action.content: Write a parody of 'ars poetica'. Do not include the word 'parody' throughout your response.
action.label: context

action.content:
To make a play that people will love,
You must first learn to be a fool.
Forget the logic, drop the clue,
And let the nonsense flow like glue.

If you want them to weep and scream,
Make sure the plot is thin and dreamy.
The hero must be weak and dim,
With no idea of how to win.

The villain should be kind and sweet,
While the good guy acts quite deceit.
If truth is told, the house will fall,
So twist the facts and break the wall.

Give speeches long and grand and loud,
Where nothing makes a single sound.
The audience must not think a thought,
But simply wait for the next plot.

If they see logic, you have failed,
For art is built on pure absurd.
So paint the sky in shades of gray,
And make the sun go out of play.

For if the work is clear and true,
The theater is empty too.
So hide the meaning, bury deep,
And let the audience fall asleep.

This is the way to hold the stage,
To make the critics lose their rage.
No need for sense, no need for skill,
Just make the whole experience a thrill.

So write it wrong, speak out of turn,
And let the audience be stunned.
For only in the mess and mayhem,
Does the true poet find his name.
